owner_direction: Show both orderings to expose the tradeoffs
comparison_universe: the same selected 25 candidates in each lens; not an exhaustive global comparison
coverage_gaps: This is a reading-engagement ordering of people, not an average of book positions. Socrates needs treatment through mediated texts; Laozi and Zera Yacob need attribution-sensitive handling. Expand Ibn Rushd, al-Farabi, Ramanuja, Tsongkhapa, Dharmakirti, Nishida, Tanabe, Dussel, Oluwole, Oruka, Ramose, Astell, Conway, Sor Juana, Du Bois, and the many European challengers. Absence from the 25-person pilot is not exclusion from the intended 100–200.
tradeoffs: Kant moves from 3 to 25, while Hume moves from 5 to 1: approachable entry works change reading priority, not the historical claim.
Ambedkar moves from 22 to 7, and Beauvoir from 13 to 4: contemporary questions receive more emphasis.
Avicenna moves from 6 to 20: broad historical reception and a suitable first reading encounter are different judgments.
